sources_considered.why: Crunchbase's own year-end data on AI's share of global venture funding. It bears on the 'drain capital' clause, but only as context.
About the Recall delay after privacy backlash. It is one product episode, so it cannot show the general claim that products got worse. Not read or cited.
A secondary summary of PitchBook. The Crunchbase primary data was preferred.

receipt.public_excerpt: AI captured close to 50% of all global funding in 2025, up from 34% in 2024, Crunchbase data shows.

evidence_items.explanation: Shows venture money concentrating in AI, which fits one reading of 'drain capital'. It does not show that total tech capital shrank, and it says nothing about product quality.

unresolved_gaps: There is no agreed measure of whether the companies' products got 'worse' because of AI.
The claim does not say whether 'drain capital' means a shift in share or an absolute decline. Total venture funding may have grown even as AI's share rose.
The normative and motive clauses cannot be measured.
The publish date given for e1 is approximate. The article was read in full text, but its exact date was not confirmed.
